description: Core deterministic engine: SQLGlot-based syntax validation for ALL statement types across dialects, schema-aware validation against the cached normalized schema (unknown table/column detection), and the rule-based optimizer (remove SELECT *, index-friendly filter hints, join checks, index recommendations). This is the heart of the product and must be thoroughly unit-tested WITHOUT any live DB or AI. Exposes /api/validate and /api/optimize (rule-based part).
steps: Create backend/app/services/validator.py: SqlValidator using sqlglot. parse(sql, dialect) with sqlglot.parse (handles multiple statements, CTEs, DDL, DML, transactions, grants, views, procedures where the parser supports). Collect ParseError -> structured syntax_errors with message and position when available. Classify each statement type. Function validate_syntax(sql, dialect) -> {statements, syntax_errors, is_valid}. Support dialects: postgres, mysql, tsql, sqlite, oracle (map friendly names).

In validator.py add validate_against_schema(parsed, normalized_schema): walk the sqlglot AST to collect referenced tables and columns (resolving aliases and CTE names which are NOT schema errors), compare against normalized schema (case-insensitive, respecting CTE/derived-table scope), produce schema_errors for unknown tables and unknown columns, and warnings (e.g. ambiguous column, column referenced without table in multi-table query). NEVER execute SQL. Return combined ValidationResult.

Create backend/app/services/optimizer.py: RuleBasedOptimizer.optimize(sql, dialect, normalized_schema) returning a list of Optimization{rule, severity, message, rewritten_sql?} plus a best-effort rewritten query. Rules: (1) SELECT * -> expand/flag to explicit needed columns using schema; (2) detect missing WHERE on UPDATE/DELETE (warning); (3) suggest indexes for columns used in WHERE/JOIN/ORDER BY that are not already indexed per schema; (4) flag leading-wildcard LIKE '%x' as non-index-friendly; (5) flag functions wrapped around indexed filter columns (non-sargable); (6) detect implicit cross joins / missing join conditions; (7) suggest LIMIT for unbounded exploratory SELECTs. Each rule is a small pure function over the AST + schema so it is unit-testable. Mark performance claims as estimates.

Create backend/app/api/validate.py: POST /api/validate (auth required) taking ValidateRequest; loads cached schema if a connection_id is given (schema errors) else syntax-only; returns ValidationResult. Create backend/app/api/optimize.py: POST /api/optimize returning rule-based optimizations and rewritten_sql; the AI part is added in FEAT-003 (leave a clearly marked integration point / call into a function that FEAT-003 fills in, defaulting to rule-based only).
Wire validate and optimize routers into main.py behind get_current_user.

Create backend/tests/test_validator.py: cover valid SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/CREATE TABLE/CTE/transaction parse as valid; malformed SQL yields syntax_errors; schema validation flags unknown table and unknown column against the fixture schema; a CTE name and table alias are NOT reported as unknown; multi-dialect parse smoke test (postgres + mysql). Assert the validator never calls any DB execute (there is no execution path).

Create backend/tests/test_optimizer.py: SELECT * on orders yields a 'select-star' optimization with a rewrite listing explicit columns; UPDATE without WHERE yields a warning; a WHERE on a non-indexed column yields an index suggestion while a WHERE on an indexed column (users.id PK) does not; LIKE '%foo' yields a non-sargable warning; a function-wrapped filter yields a non-sargable warning. Tests use the fixture NormalizedSchema only - no live DB.
Run ruff/black/pytest and fix until green.
acceptance_criteria: Validator parses all tested statement types across at least postgres and mysql dialects and reports structured syntax errors for malformed SQL
Schema validation flags unknown tables/columns but does NOT flag CTE names or aliases, using the cached normalized schema
Optimizer produces the documented rules' outputs over the fixture schema and labels performance as estimates; no code path executes SQL
ruff check and black --check still pass
verification: cd backend && uv run ruff check . && uv run black --check . && uv run pytest -q
findings:
Deterministic engine implemented. Verified: cd backend && uv run ruff check . && uv run black --check . && uv run pytest -q -> all pass (54 tests total; 25 pre-existing + 29 new across test_validator.py, test_optimizer.py, test_api_validate_optimize.py). No SQL execution path (grep confirms no .execute/cursor/connect in validator/optimizer/validate/optimize). Notes for FEAT-003:

- VALIDATOR (app/services/validator.py): class SqlValidator. Pure static analysis over the sqlglot AST. Key methods:
  * normalize_dialect(name) module fn maps friendly names -> sqlglot dialects (postgres/postgresql/pg->postgres, mysql/mariadb->mysql, tsql/sqlserver/mssql->tsql, sqlite, oracle; unknown/None -> postgres). Reuse this.
  * parse(sql, dialect) -> list[exp.Expression] (uses sqlglot.parse(read=...), filters None/empty).
  * validate_syntax(sql, dialect) -> SyntaxCheckResult(statements: list[ParsedStatement{index,statement_type,expression}], syntax_errors: list[str]); .is_valid property. statement_type is type(expr).__name__.upper() e.g. SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/CREATE.
  * validate_against_schema(parsed_expr, schema) -> (schema_errors, warnings). Resolves CTE names + table aliases as local scope (NOT errors). Unknown real tables/columns -> errors; unqualified column in multi-real-table query -> warning; ambiguous -> warning. Columns qualified by a CTE/derived alias are skipped.
  * validate(sql, dialect=None, schema=None) -> ValidationResult (app/models/api_models). THIS is the method FEAT-003 should call to re-validate every AI suggestion: validator.validate(ai_sql, dialect=req.dialect, schema=cached_schema); treat is_valid (no syntax_errors AND no schema_errors) as the gate before showing an AI suggestion as valid.

- OPTIMIZER (app/services/optimizer.py): class RuleBasedOptimizer. optimize(sql, dialect=None, schema=None) -> list[Optimization]; returns [] on parse failure (parse errors are the validator's job). rewritten_sql(findings) -> first concrete rewrite or None. Rules (each a pure module-level fn over (expr, schema), listed in RuleBasedOptimizer.RULES): rule_select_star (expands SELECT * to explicit cols when single table + schema known, sets rewritten_sql), rule_missing_where (UPDATE/DELETE w/o WHERE, severity 'error'), rule_index_suggestions (WHERE/JOIN-ON/ORDER BY columns not in index/PK; needs schema), rule_leading_wildcard_like (LIKE/ILIKE '%x' or '_x'), rule_non_sargable_function (func wrapping a column in WHERE), rule_missing_join_condition (JOIN with no ON/USING and kind != CROSS; comma-joins also become Join nodes with no 'on'), rule_unbounded_select (top-level SELECT with no LIMIT; skips bare aggregate-without-GROUP-BY). All messages label perf as '(estimate)'.

- MODELS (app/models/api_models.py): ADDED Optimization{rule,severity,message,rewritten_sql?}. OptimizeRequest now has use_ai: bool = False. OptimizeResponse reshaped: original_sql, rewritten_sql?, optimizations: list[Optimization], performance_note (default estimate text), plus NULLABLE AI fields suggested_sql/explanation/provider/is_suggestion_valid (left None by rule-based path). FEAT-003 should populate these AI fields.

- API: app/api/validate.py POST /api/validate (ValidateRequest -> ValidationResult; schema loaded only when connection_id present, 404 if unknown, 502 on load failure). app/api/optimize.py POST /api/optimize (OptimizeResponse). AI INTEGRATION POINT: optimize.py has _ai_optimize(request,user,payload,schema,response) returning None today; it is called only when payload.use_ai is True and, if it returns a non-None OptimizeResponse, that is returned instead. FEAT-003 fills _ai_optimize: build AISuggestion via provider abstraction, re-validate suggested SQL with SqlValidator.validate against the same cached schema, then set suggested_sql/explanation/provider/is_suggestion_valid. Both routers resolve a stored connection via app.api.connections.get_connection_config(sub, connection_id) (added helper) and the SchemaService from request.app.state.schema_service.
- Both routers wired in app/main.py after connections, prefix '/api', each route behind Depends(get_current_user).
- TEST FIXTURE: added `fixture_schema` fixture in tests/conftest.py (FakeAdapter schema: users(id pk,email,created_at), orders(id pk,user_id,total,status)). Reuse it. Note FakeAdapter(config) requires a ConnectionConfig arg (DBAdapter.__init__ signature).
